pr_body:
# Objective

- Add basic spatial audio support to Bevy
  - this is what rodio supports, so no HRTF, just simple stereo channel manipulation
  - no "built-in" ECS support: `Emitter` and `Listener` should be components that would automatically update the positions

This PR goal is to just expose rodio functionality, made possible with the recent update to rodio 0.16. A proper ECS integration opens a lot more questions, and would probably require an RFC

Also updates rodio and fixes #6122
pr_comments: @harudagondi could you do a quick review pass for us?
LGTM :) having two separate audio sinks looks weird to me, but it is understandable given the internal code in rodio.
Could we add another example for 2D or is it not necessary?

> Could we add another example for 2D or is it not necessary?

Added a 2d example. It can be surprising how fast attenuation happens with distance, and would happen faster in 2d with 1 pixel = 1 world unit

> > Could we add another example for 2D or is it not necessary?
> 
> Added a 2d example. It can be surprising how fast attenuation happens with distance, and would happen faster in 2d with 1 pixel = 1 world unit

It's unfortunate there isn't a way to adjust the falloff. That may result in the spatial audio not being very usable in actual game content. Would it be possible to add a simple `set_pan` function similar `set_volume`? This would probably be better suited to 2D content, and also allow users to easily implement their own spatial system.

Just tested the examples, I think there is something wrong. When running the example for the first time, the sound is at the left ear when the blue thing is near the red thing, and similarly for the green square/cube. However, rerunning the example makes it so that the audio comes out of the right when blue is near red, and vice versa. This fixes itself when I switched the examples ~(i.e. run spatial_audio_3d once is correct, two or more times is wrong, but then switching to spatial_audio_2d makes it correct, unless it is rerun for two or more times)~. This isn't even consistent. I'll try testing it more.

Currently, red outputs right ear, and green outputs left ear no matter what.

`cargo clean`ing and running the example (both 2d and 3d) fixes the issue, but is then reintroduced when running the example again (unless i `cargo clean` it again beforehand). It seems that running the examples again switches the left and right ear permanently.
Having the ears randomly reversed seems to happen for me only when running the examples in debug. It is always OK for you in release?

Just tested in `--release` and it works perfectly for me. I guess the problem only exist in debug builds? But then we would to tell the users to run the spatial audio examples in release mode. Have we mention that in the repo?

> Just tested in --release and it works perfectly for me. I guess the problem only exist in debug builds? But then we would to tell the users to run the spatial audio examples in release mode. Have we mention that in the repo?

If we want to merge this before an upstream fix, we should note this limitation in both the API docs and the example, linking to the issue you just opened.
Controversial label added due to major upstream bug. When that's fixed, it can be removed.

Added a note about the issue.

I tried to dig in rodio and failed to find an issue... I don't think it should block this PR though as people should already be compiling bevy and rodio in release
Is this provably only related to optimizations? Does the bug exist with optimized builds on very slow PCs? What about web builds optimized for binary size?
It is not safe to assume people will compile with optimizations. Can we warn when spatial audio is used in debug mode?

> It is not safe to assume people will compile with optimizations. Can we warn when spatial audio is used in debug mode?

@cart, this appears to be pre-existing; see #6122. It's obviously higher risk with this PR, but the issue isn't localized to this API.
Thats good to know. In that case, I guess we can just move forward here.

> Thats good to know. In that case, I guess we can just move forward here.

It seems the issue is random for people and not always right in release mode... if that's the case, I would prefer to wait

Rebased and patched with the `rodio` fork from @dis-da-moe

Please try and check if it's fixed for you!
waiting on https://github.com/RustAudio/rodio/pull/455
Does this address #5832? or do we need to support full HRTF for that to be considered closable?
I'd consider #5832 to be closed if there is first class ECS support for spatial audio (like adding `AudioEmitter` and `AudioListener` components to entities).
This is still blocked on a Rodio release right?

Yup...
They could update soonish to follow `cpal` update though 🤞

issue_context.title: Audio channels are sometimes reversed
issue_context.body: ## Bevy version main, 0.8.1 ## Relevant system information macOS 12.6 Macbook Pro (M1 Max) ## What you did Modified the audio example to play this sound: [RL.zip](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/files/9669090/RL.zip) ``` cargo run --example audio --release ``` ## What went wrong This audio file consists of some tones alternating from right->left->right->left. However, when played with bevy, I hear left->right->left->right This behavior is not consistent. Without `--release`, the audio plays in the correct channels.
comments:
It seems likely that this is an issue upstream with rodio or cpal.

I found the same behavior in a rodio example (also tested a wav rather than an ogg). https://github.com/RustAudio/rodio/issues/444

But a quick and dirty attempt in cpal didn't produce the same behavior.
Interesting: this was discovered in #6028. Apparently it's a pre-existing issue.

review_comments:
So the audio volume at both sinks is controlled by the listener `Transform` with respect to the emitter?

I would expect some explanations about how much the amplitude of the sound decreases with respect to distance, or to be able to adjust how much the volume drops w.r.t distance. 
(e.g. have a function volume = 1/distance or something)

I might have missed something but it looks like right now there's no way to control it? (which is fine for now, but it could be helpful to mention that the amplitude is directly connected to the distance between listener/emitter by a rodio-specific function)
rodio doesn't offer control on that

This may be a more accurate description here:

`bevy_audio` is not using HRTF for spatial audio, but is transforming the sound to a mono track, and then changing the level of each stereo channel according to the distance between the emitter and each ear by amplifying the difference between what the two ears hear.
